turns.query: But turbidity is up — doesn't that mean nutrients are up?

relevant.evidence:
Critically, particles carry adsorbed pollutants — phosphorus, metals, hydrocarbons,
pathogens — so a turbidity spike is also a proxy for contaminant loading.

Turbidity as a contaminant carrier: Sediment transports adsorbed nutrients, metals, and
pathogens — a turbidity spike can stand in for a loading event even when chemistry looks
stable.

Such turbidity data can be used for watershed investigations; for
example, for determination of visual impairment (Davies-Colley and
Smith, 2001), for correlation with concentrations of suspended
sediment, total phosphorus, or other chemical constituents, and
indicator bacteria
